test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 2nd December 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A boat running downstream covers a distance of 12 km in 30 minutes and while running upstream at the same speed, it covers the same distance in 36 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
solution:
Given:

At downstream, covers a distance of 12 km in 30 minutes 

At upstream, at the same speed, covers 12 km in 36 minutes.

Concept used:

Upstream speed = (B - R) km/h

Downstream speed = (B + R) km/h

Where, B = Speed of the boat in still water

R = Speed of the stream

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Let, the speed of the boat in still water and that of the stream be B and R km/h respectively.

According to the question,

(B + R) × 30/60 = 12

⇒ (B + R) = 12/0.5

⇒ (B + R) = 24 ....(1)

(B - R) × 36/60 = 12

⇒ (B - R) = 12 × 60/36

⇒ (B - R) = 20 ....(2)

Now, (1) + (2),

B + R + B - R = 24 + 20

⇒ 2B = 44

⇒ B = 44/2 = 22 km/h

∴ The speed of the boat in still water is 22 km/h.
